title: Active-Active Disaster Recovery: Why Standby Sites Are the Wrong Model for AI Infrastructure
summary: How active-active disaster recovery keeps every GPU working with no failover delay.
body_markdown:
Traditional disaster recovery for AI infrastructure usually means a standby site: a second facility that sits idle, waiting for something to go wrong at the primary site. It's a huge investment that spends most of its life doing nothing, and when a disaster does happen, there's still a recovery window before workloads are back online.


‍


Active-active disaster recovery removes that tradeoff. Instead of one site running production and a second site running nothing, both sites carry live traffic at the same time. If one fails, the other keeps running, no failover delay, no idle capacity paid for and unused.


‍


‍


## Why Standby Disaster Recovery **Falls Short for AI Workloads**


‍


A standby DR site solves one problem: it gives you somewhere to go if the primary site fails. But it creates two others. First, it's a standing cost: capacity purchased and maintained specifically to not be used under normal conditions. Second, it still introduces a recovery gap. Migrating workloads to a standby site, even a well-rehearsed one, takes time, and for long-running AI training and inference jobs, that gap can mean restarting from a checkpoint or losing GPU-hours that can't be recovered.


‍


As WhiteFiber Head Design Architect Toby Ford puts it, the Continuum architecture relies on all resources being active at the same time, a fully active solution, with no standby resources and nothing unused. That active posture is what makes fast recovery possible, and it's what makes sure every resource and asset paid for is actually in use.


‍


‍


## How WhiteFiber Continuum™ Delivers **Active-Active Disaster Recovery**


‍


[WhiteFiber Continuum](https://www.whitefiber.com/blog/continuum-launch) links QTS ATL1 (Atlanta) and QTS SUW1 (Suwanee) facilities, 83 kilometers apart, over 12 dark fiber strands leased from Zayo, delivering` 136 Tbps of aggregate bandwidth at 0.9 milliseconds of round-trip latency` across that span. Both facilities are HITRUST-certified, and both run 256 NVIDIA H200 GPUs each, 512 total, active-active rather than primary-and-standby.


‍


The network fabric, DriveNets AI Fabric running on Broadcom's Jericho3-AI and Ramon3 chipsets, uses scheduled cell-based Ethernet with HBM-buffered leaf switches at the boundary between each site's internal fabric and the[inter-site link](https://www.whitefiber.com/blog/cross-data-center-networking-solution) . On the storage side, WEKA NeuralMesh replicates data intelligently, pulling exactly what a job needs to the site where its GPU allocation lands, instead of keeping both sites in constant lockstep. That's what lets a training job continue, or restart, across sites without dragging a full duplicate copy of the dataset along with it.


‍


Because no single site is a single point of failure, a training run continues even when one location goes down, rather than stalling until it's restored. Continuity of operations becomes architectural, not procedural: there's no runbook to execute, no manual cutover, no window where production traffic has nowhere to go.


‍


‍

Toby Ford, Head Design Architect at WhiteFiber, explains how Continuum's[scale-across architecture](https://www.whitefiber.com/blog/what-is-scale-across-networking) is built to meet both uptime expectations and compliance requirements through active-active design.Watch here

We ensure that we have an appropriate amount of capacity at their disposal and then extra as needed to make sure that if any failures happen, that we can recover for any kind of disaster."


‍


‍


## Beyond Two Sites: **What Active-Active Looks Like at Scale**


‍


Continuum's active-active model is validated on two sites today, with headroom built into the underlying chipset for significantly more. The Jericho3-AI chipset already deployed supports a[single cluster of up to 32,000 GPUs](https://www.whitefiber.com/blog/multi-site-gpu-cluster) at 800Gbps each, 62 times the 512 GPUs running across ATL1 and SUW1 today. As WhiteFiber[expands into additional sites](https://www.whitefiber.com/blog/ai-data-center-power-constraints) , likely in a hub-and-spoke or mesh configuration, the same active-active principle extends: no single site carries production alone, and no site sits idle as a cold standby.


‍


‍


## Who Needs **Active-Active Disaster Recovery**


‍


Active-active disaster recovery matters most where downtime has a real cost and standby capacity is hard to justify:


‍


1. ` Regulated enterprises in finance and life sciences` , where compliance regimes require provable dual-site resiliency, not just a documented recovery plan
2. ` Frontier model labs and AI research teams` running long, expensive training jobs that can't afford to restart from a checkpoint every time one site has a bad day
3. ` GPUaaS and NeoCloud providers` that need to back an uptime SLA with architecture, not a procedural promise
4. ` Sovereign AI and government workloads` , where spinning facilities up and down as mandates change creates service interruption for the people who rely on them


‍


‍


‍

## **FAQ**


‍


#### **What is active-active disaster recovery?**


‍


> Active-active disaster recovery means two or more sites carry live production traffic at the same time, instead of one site running production and a second sitting idle as a standby. If one site fails, the others continue running without a failover delay.


‍


#### **How is it different from a standby DR site?**


‍


> A standby site is a standing investment that sits unused under normal conditions and still requires a recovery window when a disaster happens. Active-active removes both costs: there's no idle capacity, and no cutover delay, because every site is already carrying production traffic.


‍


#### **How does WhiteFiber Continuum implement it?**


‍


> Continuum runs two HITRUST-certified data centers, 83 kilometers apart, as a single active-active cluster using DriveNets AI Fabric for the network layer and WEKA NeuralMesh for data and storage. Both sites run live traffic simultaneously, so there's no single point of failure and no standby capacity sitting unused.


‍


#### **Does active-active disaster recovery compromise data sovereignty or compliance?**


‍


> No. Continuum is built to keep sensitive workloads within their originating jurisdiction even while failover and pooled compute happen across sites, so regulated enterprises get active-active resilience without giving up data residency.


‍


#### **Is it available today?**


‍


> Yes. WhiteFiber Continuum has been commercially available since September 23, 2026.


‍


#### **Can this resilient architecture scale beyond two sites?**


‍


> Yes. The Jericho3-AI chipset underneath Continuum has headroom for a single cluster of up to 32,000 GPUs, and additional sites are expected to join in a hub-and-spoke or mesh configuration using the same active-active approach already in place.
